To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the N-terminal cytoplasmic tail of ATP7B is metallated by Cu1-HAH1 and that the energetics for Cu(I) transfer from the copper chaperone to ATP7B differ from the analogous energetics for ATP7A.
the interaction of copper(I)-HA1 with the N-terminal tail of ATP7B is distinct from that with ATP7A, and that this difference is related to the distinct functional roles of these two ATPases.
the interaction of Cu(I)-HA1H with the N-terminal tail of ATP7B is different from that with ATP7A and is likely to play an important role in copper(I) transfer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of the copper chaperone HAH1 with the N-terminal cytoplasmic tail of ATP7B, which is a crucial step in the copper(I) homeostat of eukaryotic cells.
the interaction of a copper(I) chaperone with a protein tail that is capable of binding multiple copper(I) ions.
the role of the N-terminal domain of ATP7B in the copper(I)-HA1H1 interaction and its relevance to the copper(I) transport process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the copper chaperone HAH1 binds to the N-terminal tail of the ATPase ATP7B, but that this interaction does not involve all six metal-binding domains.
the Wilson disease protein ATP7B has an additional copper(I)-chaperone binding site compared to the closely related protein ATP7A.

the interaction of the Wilson ATPase with copper(I)-chaperone is different from that in the Menkes ATPase and that the different behavior of the domains is likely due to the specific requirements of the different copper transporters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N-terminal cytosol tail of human ATP7B is capable of interacting with copper(I)-HAC1 in a highly specific and cooperative manner.
the N-terminal cytoplasmic tail of ATP7B is more flexible and more dynamic than the corresponding region of the ATP7A protein.
the interaction of the N-terminal tail of ATP7B with its copper(I) chaperone HAH1 is distinct from that of ATP7A, which is consistent with the different roles played by the two ATPases.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the interaction of the N-terminal domain of ATP7B with copper(I)-Hah1 is more extensive than previously anticipated, with implications for the functional mechanism of this important copper(I) transporter.

, in the context of the entire tail, the individual domains of the ATP7B tail have distinct roles in copper(I) binding, which are not reflected in the behavior of the domains in the absence of the rest of the tail.

the N-terminal tail of ATP7B is not just a collection of domains that are folded independently of one another but is instead a highly integrated functional unit that has been designed to carry out a specific task.
